easy.def: To leave something and never come back.
examples: They abandoned the old house.
Do not abandon your pet.
The boat was abandoned.

more.def: To go away and leave someone or something behind for good.
examples: The family abandoned the old farm and moved to town.
The sailors abandoned the sinking ship.
She would never abandon her pet when she moved.
The abandonment of the farm was sad.
There was abandonment.
The pup felt abandonment.

more.def: The act of leaving someone or something behind and not coming back.
examples: The abandonment of the old farm was sad.
The town suffered from the abandonment of its mill.
A gentle shelter helps animals that suffer abandonment.

easy.def: The belly, or the middle part of your body below the chest.
examples: My abdomen hurts.
The doctor checked my abdomen.
I held my abdomen when I laughed.

more.def: The part of the body between the chest and the legs, where the stomach is; also the back part of an insect.
examples: The doctor pressed gently on my abdomen.
Exercises like sit-ups make the muscles in your abdomen strong.
The bee's abdomen has black and yellow stripes.
Sit-ups work the abdominal muscles.
She had abdominal pain.
The doctor looked at his abdominal area.

more.def: Having to do with the abdomen, or belly area.
examples: Sit-ups strengthen the abdominal muscles.
She had a slight abdominal pain after lunch.
The nurse checked the abdominal area of the patient.
We abide by the rules.
Players abide by the rules.
She abided by the law.

more.def: To accept and follow a rule or a decision, or to put up with something.
examples: All the swimmers must abide by the pool rules.
We agreed to abide by the judge's decision.
I cannot abide the sound of chalk squeaking on the board.
She has the ability to swim fast.
Birds have the ability to fly.
He has the ability to draw well.

more.def: The power or skill to do something.
examples: Dolphins have the ability to talk to each other with clicks.
Her ability to remember names surprised her new teacher.
A good swimmer needs strength and the ability to stay calm.

easy.def: On fire, or shining very brightly.
examples: The barn was ablaze.
The sky was ablaze with color.
The tree was ablaze with lights.

more.def: On fire, or shining brightly with light or color.
examples: The old barn was ablaze, and the firefighters rushed to put it out.
The sky was ablaze with orange and red at sunset.
The streets were ablaze with lights for the holiday.

easy.def: Having the power or skill to do something.
examples: I am able to tie my shoes.
Are you able to swim?
He was able to lift the box.

more.def: Having the strength, skill or chance to do something.
examples: Birds are able to fly long distances.
I was not able to come because I was sick.
She was able to solve the riddle in two minutes.
An abnormal sound came from the car.
The weather is abnormal.
It was abnormal to see snow in June.

more.def: Different from what is usual or expected, often in a way that is worrying.
examples: Snow in June is abnormal for our town.
The doctor checked the abnormal sound in the engine.
It was abnormal for the dog to refuse his dinner.

easy.def: On a boat, train, plane or bus.
examples: All aboard!
The kids are aboard.
We went aboard the ship.

more.def: On or onto a ship, train, plane or bus.
examples: The passengers climbed aboard the ferry.
Welcome aboard, said the pilot.
The captain called for everyone to come aboard.
They abolish the rule.
The town abolished the tax.
They will abolish the law.

more.def: To put a complete end to a rule or custom.
examples: The school abolished the old rule.
Long ago, people worked to abolish unfair laws.
The town abolished the tax on bikes.
The weather was abominable.
An abominable smell.
The abominable snowman.

more.def: Very bad or terrible.
examples: The weather was abominable, with rain and wind.
An abominable smell came from the old fridge.
The abominable snowman is a make-believe giant.
This book is about frogs.
Tell me about your day.
We talked about the trip.

more.def: On the subject of something, or having to do with it.
examples: We read a story about a boy who builds a boat.
The scientist gave a talk about volcanoes.
What are you thinking about?
It is about noon.
I have about five stickers.
She is about as tall as me.

more.def: Close to a number or amount, but not exact.
examples: The walk to the park takes about ten minutes.
About twenty children came to the picnic.
The pond is about three feet deep.
The bird is above the tree.
The clock is above the door.
Fly above the clouds.

more.def: At a higher place than something else.
examples: The plane flew above the clouds.
A picture hangs above the fireplace.
The moon rose above the hills.
The stars above are bright.
Look at the sky above.
See the picture above.

more.def: In or to a higher place.
examples: The clouds above turned dark.
Read the paragraph above.
Birds circled above.

easy.def: A magic word that magicians say.
examples: The magician said abracadabra!
Abracadabra, the rabbit is gone!
Say abracadabra.

more.def: A word said by magicians as they do a trick.
examples: The magician waved his wand and said "Abracadabra!"
"Abracadabra!" she shouted, and out popped a flower.
Children chanted "abracadabra" at the magic show.
We traveled abroad.
She lives abroad.
He studied abroad.

more.def: In or to a foreign country.
examples: We traveled abroad last summer.
My aunt lives abroad.
He studied abroad in France.
The bus made an abrupt stop.
The song had an abrupt end.
She gave an abrupt answer.

more.def: Sudden and unexpected, or short and rude.
examples: The bus made an abrupt stop, and we all lurched forward.
The song came to an abrupt end.
His abrupt answer made me stop talking.
The music stopped abruptly.
The bus stopped abruptly.
He left abruptly.

more.def: In a way that is sudden and surprising.
examples: The road ended abruptly at the edge of the cliff.
The bus stopped abruptly, and we all jerked forward.
She abruptly left the room.
Her absence was noticed.
The teacher marked his absence.
The absence was long.

more.def: A time when someone or something is not in a place where they should be.
examples: Her absence from school was noticed.
His absence from the team was a big loss.
In the absence of rain, the plants dried up.
Sam was absent today.
Three kids are absent.
She is absent from school.

more.def: Not present at a place where you are expected to be, such as school or a meeting.
examples: Sam was absent from school today because he had a cold.
Two players were absent from the team practice.
The teacher marked who was absent in her book.
It was an absolute mess.
I have absolute trust in her.
There was absolute silence.

more.def: Complete, with nothing left out.
examples: The room was in absolute silence.
I have absolute trust in my best friend.
It was an absolute mess after the party.
I am absolutely sure.
The room was absolutely quiet.
It was absolutely delicious.

more.def: Completely and without any doubt.
examples: The soup was absolutely delicious.
I am absolutely certain that I locked the door.
The night was absolutely silent.
A sponge can absorb water.
The towel absorbs the water on the floor.
Dry dirt absorbs the rain.

more.def: To take in or soak up something, such as a liquid, heat, or light.
examples: Dark clothes absorb more heat from the sun than light clothes.
Plant roots absorb water from the soil.
Thick curtains absorbed most of the noise from the street.
The idea is absurd.
The joke was absurd.
He wore an absurd hat.

more.def: So silly that it makes no sense.
examples: The idea of a cat driving a car is absurd.
He wore an absurd hat with a feather.
The story was so absurd that we laughed.
The garden had an abundance of flowers.
There was an abundance of food.
We have an abundance of apples.

more.def: A very large amount of something.
examples: An abundance of rain made the grass grow tall.
There was an abundance of food at the picnic.
An abundance of rain made the grass grow.

easy.def: A very deep hole that seems to have no bottom.
examples: We looked into the abyss.
A dark abyss.
The abyss is deep.

more.def: A very deep hole or gap that seems to have no bottom.
examples: The explorers looked down into the dark abyss.
A deep abyss lay beneath the old bridge.
The ocean has abysses that are miles deep.
